nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: Start 1.25 mg orally once daily; titrate every 2‑4 weeks to target 5 mg once daily (or maximum tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually after each titration step
medications.purpose: Renin‑angiotensin system blockade to reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I or ARB for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CV risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 0.1 U/kg subcutaneously once daily (adjust based on fasting glucose)
medications.duration: Indefinite – titrate to fasting glucose 4–7 mmol/L; review every 2 weeks until stable
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control; insulin is the preferred agent when eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NG203 indicates insulin as safe glucose‑lowering therapy in advanced CKD; metformin contraindicated

medications.dose: 0.05 U/kg subcutaneously before each main meal (adjust based on post‑prandial glucose)
medications.duration: Indefinite – titrate to post‑prandial <10 mmol/L; review with basal insulin adjustments
medications.purpose: Prandial glucose control in combination with basal insulin
medications.nice_justification: NG203 supports intensive insulin regimens for type 2 diabetes with CKD‑5

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interaction
No chronic interaction; epinephrine may transiently raise blood pressure during anaphylaxis
interactions_checked.action: Patient education to monitor BP after emergency epinephrine use

interactions_checked.interaction: Both metabolised by CYP3A4; loratadine is a weak inhibitor, unlikely to cause clinically relevant increase in atorvastatin levels at 20 mg
interactions_checked.action: No dose change required; monitor for rare myopathy if other strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are added

interactions_checked.interaction: Epinephrine can raise blood glucose acutely, potentially counteracting insulin effect
interactions_checked.action: Advise patient to check glucose after using epinephrine and adjust insulin if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR 12 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis
CKD‑5; NSAIDs accelerate renal decline and cause fluid retention
Dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use non‑contrast imaging or apply renal protective measures if contrast unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, bicarbonate, and calcium/phosphate levels are not available – order before initiating Ramipril and monitor K⁺ after each dose change.
Blood pressure values are missing – assume uncontrolled or ≥130/80 mmHg; target <130/80 mmHg per NG203.
Lipid profile (LDL‑C) not provided – start moderate‑intensity atorvastatin (20 mg) and adjust based on results.
HbA1c and fasting glucose not available – insulin regimen is initiated with standard weight‑based dosing and will be titrated to glucose targets.
No data on prior ACE‑I tolerance or angio‑edema history – assume no contraindication but monitor for cough or swelling.
Patient is not yet on dialysis; dosing assumes pre‑dialysis CKD‑5.
treatment_summary: Start renin‑angiotensin blockade with low‑dose Ramipril and titrate to 5 mg daily, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg for CV risk reduction, and commence a basal‑bolus insulin regimen (glargine + aspart) for glycaemic control, all in line with NICE NG203. Avoid metformin, NSAIDs, and dual ACE‑I/ARB therapy. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, BP, lipids, and glucose regularly, and adjust therapy as labs become available.
